  # ===========================================================================
  # REPAIR R1 (closes J1): the Stage A enumerated space must BE the true
  # L(S,2), not a proper subgroup of it.
  # ===========================================================================
  repair_r1_stage_a_true_selmer_enumeration:
    closes_finding: 'J1 (validator, TASK-20260831-234e80, DISSENT)'
    addresses_repair: 'R1 of DEC-20260831-fada1e'
    repair_diff_note: >-
      DIFF AGAINST protocol.search_boundary.stage_a_selmer_computation
      (predecessor lines ~899-949). The predecessor's enumeration_order
      indexed "the 2^|S_L| classes of L(S,2)... by the bit-vector of
      exponents (0 or 1) over S_L", i.e. it identified L(S,2) with the group
      generated purely by the primes of L above S, dimension exactly |S_L|.
      J1's worked_attack showed this is FALSE: by Dirichlet's S-unit
      theorem, dim_F2(O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2) = |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e,
      where rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1 >= 1 for any cubic field (r1+2r2=3 admits
      no integer solution with r1+r2<=1), and e in {0,1} is a torsion
      correction (from the root of unity -1). The predecessor's procedure
      never constructs or tests the rank(O_L^*)-dimensional unit-group
      directions, so a literal implementation tests a proper subgroup and a
      reported "dim = 31" would not be the exact dim Sel_2(E) the decision
      gate needs. This repair replaces the tracked_object, enumeration_order,
      and decision_gate wholesale with the specification below, and
      re-derives the cost model from it rather than from the wrong bitvector
      count.
    true_object_specification: >-
      L(S,2) IS DEFINED AS O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2, the group of S-units of
      L modulo squares, where O_{L,S} is the ring of S-integers of L (the
      elements of L integral away from S_L, the primes of L above S) and
      O_{L,S}^* its unit group. This is the ambient group the connecting
      homomorphism of full 2-descent actually lands its image inside, per
      the standard S-unit-theoretic treatment of 2-descent via a resolvent
      cubic (Cohen, "A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory",
      chapters 4 and 6 on S-unit and class-group computation; Cremona,
      Fisher and Stoll's descent literature on practical Selmer-group
      computation via S-unit groups; provenance recalled, a genuine Stage-0
      verification obligation, not asserted as executed fact here). It sits
      in the standard exact sequence of S-unit theory (recalled, e.g. Cohen
      ACANT Theorem 4.9.5-style statement, restated for the reader rather
      than re-derived from scratch in this design document):
      1 -> O_L^*/(O_L^*)^2 -> O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2 -> (F2-vector space
      generated by the classes of the primes of S_L in Cl(L)) -> ...,
      whose consequence for the DIMENSION (not the explicit generators) is:
      dim_F2 L(S,2) = |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e, where rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1
      is GIVEN BY DIRICHLET'S UNIT THEOREM PURELY FROM THE SIGNATURE (r1,r2)
      of L and requires NO class-group computation to determine (only a
      count of real vs. complex embeddings of the resolvent cubic, itself
      decidable cheaply by Sturm's theorem sign-counting on the cubic's real
      roots -- a finite, elementary computation, not a number-field
      algorithm). What DOES depend on class-group data is not the DIMENSION
      but the EXPLICIT GENERATING SET needed to actually write down and
      locally-test each class, which is where h(L) enters, per
      generating_set_specification below.
    generating_set_specification: >-
      To enumerate L(S,2) concretely (not merely know its dimension), Stage
      A' requires an explicit generating set for O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2,
      consisting of three families: (i) a fundamental system of units of
      O_L^* (rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1 generators, plus -1 for the torsion unit
      e), obtainable in principle by a unit-group algorithm (e.g. the
      recalled standard approach via the class group and regulator
      computation, or the LLL-based unit-finding methods surveyed in Cohen
      ACANT ch. 6); (ii) for each prime p of S_L that is PRINCIPAL in O_L
      (generator pi_p directly computable once known principal), pi_p
      itself; (iii) for each prime p of S_L that is NON-PRINCIPAL, a
      generator of p^n for n the order of the ideal class [p] in Cl(L) --
      this REQUIRES knowing Cl(L) (or at least the subgroup generated by
      the classes of S_L's primes) and solving the associated principal-
      ideal-generator subproblem for that power. WHEN h(L) = 1 (class
      number one), every prime of L is principal, family (iii) is vacuous,
      and no class-group computation is needed at all beyond confirming
      h(L)=1 itself. WHEN h(L) > 1, family (iii) is unavoidable and its cost
      is dominated by computing Cl(L) (or a sufficient piece of it) --
      exactly the class-group data DEC-20260831-fada1e's R1 names.
    honest_cost_model: >-
      RE-DERIVED FROM THE TRUE COMPUTATION, replacing
      target_complexity.time_exponent's Stage A figure and
      budgets_and_stops.stage_a_selmer_computation's work_units/budget
      wholesale (superseded, see supersession_map). Two cost components,
      not one: (A) the ENUMERATION cost, now over 2^(|S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e)
      classes rather than 2^|S_L| -- for a cubic field, rank(O_L^*) is 1
      (signature (1,1)) or 2 (signature (3,0)), plus e in {0,1}, so this
      enlarges the predecessor's exponent by at most 3, a MODEST change in
      the same complexity class (still exponential in |S_L|, not a new
      complexity regime) once R2's corrected |S| = 20 (repair_r2) is also
      applied. (B) the GENERATING-SET cost -- computing O_L^*, and, if
      h(L) > 1, Cl(L) and explicit principal-ideal generators for the
      non-principal primes of S_L -- which the predecessor's cost model
      DID NOT INCLUDE AT ALL (it costed only the bitvector enumeration).
      This second component is the dominant, and potentially decisive,
      new cost term.
    feasibility_finding_stated_plainly: >-
      STATED PLAINLY, PER THE REPAIR'S OWN INSTRUCTION. Component (B) above
      is, at curve 302's actual scale, LIKELY INFEASIBLE with any presently
      known algorithm within a realistic Coordinator-approvable budget, and
      this document says so rather than asserting Stage A' as routinely
      executable. Grounds for this finding, disclosed as an order-of-
      magnitude argument from already-frozen, already-verified numbers
      (bad_primes' largest entry has ~81 decimal digits per the frozen JSON,
      and the frozen discriminant string is ~204 decimal digits; disc(L),
      for the resolvent cubic's discriminant, is tied to Delta_E by
      repair_r3.resolvent_cubic_identity's corrected exact identity and is
      therefore comparably large, on the order of 10^200, i.e. roughly a
      664-bit quantity) -- NOT a claim that any computation was performed:
      the best presently known algorithms for computing class groups and
      unit groups of a number field (Buchmann-type index-calculus methods,
      Hafner-McCurley, and their GRH-conditional accelerations) run in
      SUBEXPONENTIAL time in the field's discriminant, L_disc[1/2, c]-type
      complexity (recalled, standard computational algebraic number theory;
      Cohen ACANT ch. 6, Buchmann 1990). At a ~664-bit discriminant, this
      subexponential cost is of the SAME ORDER OF DIFFICULTY as factoring an
      RSA modulus or solving a discrete log problem of comparable bit
      length -- i.e., precisely the class of problem this research program
      studies as currently intractable at cryptographic scale. Unconditional
      algorithms (avoiding GRH) are categorically worse, typically requiring
      an explicit Minkowski-bound ideal enumeration whose bound itself grows
      with sqrt(disc(L)), which at this scale is astronomically larger still.
      THIS FINDING IS A DESIGN-TIME ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASURED RESULT: no
      dry-run cost probe for the class-group computation has been run (that
      would be execution, forbidden in this task), and a future
      Coordinator-authorized bounded probe could in principle contradict
      this estimate (e.g. if L happens to have h(L) = 1, which is not
      determinable without running the probe). It is recorded here as the
      honest expectation, not as a proven impossibility.
    decidable_fallback_stage_a_prime_repaired: >-
      WHAT REMAINS DECIDABLE, restructuring Stage A into three gated
      sub-stages, replacing the predecessor's single-stage
      enumeration_order/halting_condition/decision_gate wholesale:
      Stage A'.0 (cheap, unconditional): compute the signature (r1,r2) of L
      via Sturm's-theorem sign-counting on the real roots of the resolvent
      cubic (an elementary, finite computation, no number-field algorithm
      needed), fixing rank(O_L^*) in closed form with no class-group work.
      Stage A'.1 (bounded-effort, may fail): attempt to compute h(L) and
      Cl(L)[2] (or at minimum, whether each prime of S_L is principal, and
      if not, a generator of the appropriate power) via a DECLARED,
      BUDGETED class-group/unit-group computation. If this bound is
      exhausted before completion -- EXPECTED at curve 302's scale per
      feasibility_finding_stated_plainly above, but never assumed without
      running the bounded attempt -- Stage A' reports "class group and
      S-unit generating set undetermined within declared budget" (an
      honest, scoped, non-mathematical-evidence outcome, AGENTS.md rule 3)
      and HALTS at this gate: Stage A'.2 does not run and READING (a)
      closure is UNREACHABLE via this route for curve 302.
      Stage A'.2 (only if A'.1 succeeds): full L(S,2) enumeration with
      explicit generators from generating_set_specification, local
      solubility testing exactly as the predecessor's enumeration_order
      described for the S_L-generated part, extended over the full
      generating set; produces an EXACT dim Sel_2(E), and READING (a) /
      READING (b) apply exactly as the predecessor's idea.claim states
      (decision_rule_integrity below).
      Stage A'.3 (always available, regardless of A'.1's outcome): the
      predecessor's ORIGINAL literal S_L-bitvector procedure is RETAINED but
      RELABELED HONESTLY as testing only the SUBGROUP W of L(S,2) generated
      by the S_L-prime classes that are individually principal (each
      non-principal prime's class is simply DROPPED from W, shrinking it
      further rather than corrupting it), producing an UNCONDITIONAL LOWER
      BOUND: dim(W) <= dim Sel_2(E) <= dim L(S,2). This lower bound CAN
      license Stage B (READING (b)'s search-licensing half only) if
      dim(W tested everywhere-locally-soluble) already reaches 32, but it
      CAN NEVER be used for READING (a) closure, since it may miss classes
      exactly as J1 found for the predecessor's original procedure.
    interaction_with_r2: >-
      Stage A'.1/A'.2's enumeration size and Stage A'.3's fallback size both
      depend on |S_L|, which repair_r2.corrected_prime_set_construction
      below fixes at <= 60 (not the predecessor's <= 63); this repair's cost
      model uses the corrected bound.
    added_interpretation_limit: >-
      ADDITIVE to protocol.interpretation_limits (inherited unchanged, not
      replaced): a negative or undetermined Stage A'.1 outcome is NEVER
      evidence for or against rank 32 (AGENTS.md rule 3), and specifically
      is NOT the same non-result as a Stage A'.2 budget-ceiling halt on the
      enumeration itself -- the two failure points (class-group computation
      vs. local-solubility enumeration) must be reported distinctly, since a
      reader conflating them could wrongly believe the enumeration itself
      was attempted and failed rather than never having reached the
      enumeration stage.
    what_remains_open: >-
      Whether Stage A'.1 is actually tractable for curve 302's real L is
      OPEN and cannot be resolved without running the bounded probe
      (explicitly out of scope for this zero-execution repair). If it is
      confirmed intractable, whether any alternative unconditional route to
      Cl(L)[2] exists at this scale (e.g. analytic bounds, partial descent-
      compatible workarounds, or accepting a GRH-conditional generating set
      with an explicit heuristic flag rather than an unconditional one) is
      an OPEN design question, deferred to a future proposal rather than
      resolved here.

  # ===========================================================================
  # REPAIR R2 (closes J4): true set union for S; |S| = 20 for curve 302;
  # propagate into |S_L|.
  # ===========================================================================
  repair_r2_corrected_prime_set_construction:
    closes_finding: 'J4 (validator, TASK-20260831-234e80, DISSENT)'
    addresses_repair: 'R2 of DEC-20260831-fada1e'
    repair_diff_note: >-
      DIFF AGAINST every predecessor restatement of "|S| <= 21 (20 listed
      bad primes plus 2)" (object_first_analysis lines ~205-210, idea.claim
      lines ~279-280, target_complexity lines ~752-753, search_boundary
      lines ~910-912). J4's worked_attack checked the frozen JSON's
      bad_primes array directly: it has exactly 20 entries and the FIRST
      entry is already "2". S = {2} union {primes dividing Delta(E)} is
      therefore S = bad_primes AS A SET, |S| = 20, not 21 -- the
      predecessor's phrasing treated "2" as an additional element beyond
      the 20-entry list, double-counting it.
    corrected_construction: >-
      S IS CONSTRUCTED AS A TRUE SET UNION, not a list concatenation:
      S := {p in Z : p prime, p | Delta(E)} union {2}, computed by first
      building the set of DISTINCT prime factors of Delta(E) (a Stage-0
      verification obligation already required by
      baseline_reproduction.assumptions, inherited unchanged: confirming
      the frozen bad_primes list is the complete, multiplicity-free
      factorisation), then taking the UNION with {2} using idempotent set
      semantics -- i.e., using an actual set/frozenset data structure (or a
      sorted, de-duplicated list with an explicit dedup step performed
      BEFORE the canonical ascending sort that enumeration_order requires),
      never string or list concatenation of "{2}" with bad_primes. For
      curve 302 specifically: since bad_primes already contains "2" as its
      first entry, S = bad_primes exactly and |S| = 20. This is stated as a
      curve-302-specific fact (verified directly against the frozen JSON in
      this session, no execution required -- reading and comparing a
      20-entry array to itself), NOT as a general claim that 2 is always
      already present in bad_primes for every curve; the construction
      formula above is the general, always-correct rule, and its output for
      curve 302 happens to equal bad_primes because of this curve's
      specific factorisation.
    propagated_bound: >-
      |S_L| <= 3*|S| = 3*20 = 60 (not the predecessor's <= 63), since each
      rational prime splits into at most 3 primes of the cubic field L.
      Combined with repair_r1's honest_cost_model, the full ambient
      enumeration dimension is <= |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e <= 60 + 2 + 1 = 63
      -- numerically close to the predecessor's original (wrong-reasoned)
      bound of 63 by coincidence, but now for the CORRECT reason (the true
      ambient space including units), not the incorrect one (double-counted
      prime 2).
    duplicate_element_ambiguity_removed: >-
      The predecessor's enumeration_order instruction to "sort S in
      ascending numeric order" was ambiguous about whether S was a genuine
      set (2 appears once) or a concatenation (2 could appear twice,
      corrupting the canonical sort and double-processing 2's splitting
      behavior in L). This repair removes the ambiguity: S is constructed
      as a set (see corrected_construction), so this failure mode cannot
      occur by construction, independent of implementation care.
    what_remains_open: >-
      None. This repair is a closed arithmetic/construction fix with no
      remaining open mathematical question; it does not depend on any
      future computation to validate (the frozen bad_primes array is
      already fully specified and was checked directly in this session).

  # ===========================================================================
  # REPAIR R1 (closes J1): the Stage A enumerated space must BE the true
  # L(S,2), not a proper subgroup of it.
  # ===========================================================================
  repair_r1_stage_a_true_selmer_enumeration:
    closes_finding: 'J1 (validator, TASK-20260831-234e80, DISSENT)'
    addresses_repair: 'R1 of DEC-20260831-fada1e'
    repair_diff_note: >-
      DIFF AGAINST protocol.search_boundary.stage_a_selmer_computation
      (predecessor lines ~899-949). The predecessor's enumeration_order
      indexed "the 2^|S_L| classes of L(S,2)... by the bit-vector of
      exponents (0 or 1) over S_L", i.e. it identified L(S,2) with the group
      generated purely by the primes of L above S, dimension exactly |S_L|.
      J1's worked_attack showed this is FALSE: by Dirichlet's S-unit
      theorem, dim_F2(O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2) = |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e,
      where rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1 >= 1 for any cubic field (r1+2r2=3 admits
      no integer solution with r1+r2<=1), and e in {0,1} is a torsion
      correction (from the root of unity -1). The predecessor's procedure
      never constructs or tests the rank(O_L^*)-dimensional unit-group
      directions, so a literal implementation tests a proper subgroup and a
      reported "dim = 31" would not be the exact dim Sel_2(E) the decision
      gate needs. This repair replaces the tracked_object, enumeration_order,
      and decision_gate wholesale with the specification below, and
      re-derives the cost model from it rather than from the wrong bitvector
      count.
    true_object_specification: >-
      L(S,2) IS DEFINED AS O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2, the group of S-units of
      L modulo squares, where O_{L,S} is the ring of S-integers of L (the
      elements of L integral away from S_L, the primes of L above S) and
      O_{L,S}^* its unit group. This is the ambient group the connecting
      homomorphism of full 2-descent actually lands its image inside, per
      the standard S-unit-theoretic treatment of 2-descent via a resolvent
      cubic (Cohen, "A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory",
      chapters 4 and 6 on S-unit and class-group computation; Cremona,
      Fisher and Stoll's descent literature on practical Selmer-group
      computation via S-unit groups; provenance recalled, a genuine Stage-0
      verification obligation, not asserted as executed fact here). It sits
      in the standard exact sequence of S-unit theory (recalled, e.g. Cohen
      ACANT Theorem 4.9.5-style statement, restated for the reader rather
      than re-derived from scratch in this design document):
      1 -> O_L^*/(O_L^*)^2 -> O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2 -> (F2-vector space
      generated by the classes of the primes of S_L in Cl(L)) -> ...,
      whose consequence for the DIMENSION (not the explicit generators) is:
      dim_F2 L(S,2) = |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e, where rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1
      is GIVEN BY DIRICHLET'S UNIT THEOREM PURELY FROM THE SIGNATURE (r1,r2)
      of L and requires NO class-group computation to determine (only a
      count of real vs. complex embeddings of the resolvent cubic, itself
      decidable cheaply by Sturm's theorem sign-counting on the cubic's real
      roots -- a finite, elementary computation, not a number-field
      algorithm). What DOES depend on class-group data is not the DIMENSION
      but the EXPLICIT GENERATING SET needed to actually write down and
      locally-test each class, which is where h(L) enters, per
      generating_set_specification below.
    generating_set_specification: >-
      To enumerate L(S,2) concretely (not merely know its dimension), Stage
      A' requires an explicit generating set for O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2,
      consisting of three families: (i) a fundamental system of units of
      O_L^* (rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1 generators, plus -1 for the torsion unit
      e), obtainable in principle by a unit-group algorithm (e.g. the
      recalled standard approach via the class group and regulator
      computation, or the LLL-based unit-finding methods surveyed in Cohen
      ACANT ch. 6); (ii) for each prime p of S_L that is PRINCIPAL in O_L
      (generator pi_p directly computable once known principal), pi_p
      itself; (iii) for each prime p of S_L that is NON-PRINCIPAL, a
      generator of p^n for n the order of the ideal class [p] in Cl(L) --
      this REQUIRES knowing Cl(L) (or at least the subgroup generated by
      the classes of S_L's primes) and solving the associated principal-
      ideal-generator subproblem for that power. WHEN h(L) = 1 (class
      number one), every prime of L is principal, family (iii) is vacuous,
      and no class-group computation is needed at all beyond confirming
      h(L)=1 itself. WHEN h(L) > 1, family (iii) is unavoidable and its cost
      is dominated by computing Cl(L) (or a sufficient piece of it) --
      exactly the class-group data DEC-20260831-fada1e's R1 names.
    honest_cost_model: >-
      RE-DERIVED FROM THE TRUE COMPUTATION, replacing
      target_complexity.time_exponent's Stage A figure and
      budgets_and_stops.stage_a_selmer_computation's work_units/budget
      wholesale (superseded, see supersession_map). Two cost components,
      not one: (A) the ENUMERATION cost, now over 2^(|S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e)
      classes rather than 2^|S_L| -- for a cubic field, rank(O_L^*) is 1
      (signature (1,1)) or 2 (signature (3,0)), plus e in {0,1}, so this
      enlarges the predecessor's exponent by at most 3, a MODEST change in
      the same complexity class (still exponential in |S_L|, not a new
      complexity regime) once R2's corrected |S| = 20 (repair_r2) is also
      applied. (B) the GENERATING-SET cost -- computing O_L^*, and, if
      h(L) > 1, Cl(L) and explicit principal-ideal generators for the
      non-principal primes of S_L -- which the predecessor's cost model
      DID NOT INCLUDE AT ALL (it costed only the bitvector enumeration).
      This second component is the dominant, and potentially decisive,
      new cost term.
    feasibility_finding_stated_plainly: >-
      STATED PLAINLY, PER THE REPAIR'S OWN INSTRUCTION. Component (B) above
      is, at curve 302's actual scale, LIKELY INFEASIBLE with any presently
      known algorithm within a realistic Coordinator-approvable budget, and
      this document says so rather than asserting Stage A' as routinely
      executable. Grounds for this finding, disclosed as an order-of-
      magnitude argument from already-frozen, already-verified numbers
      (bad_primes' largest entry has ~81 decimal digits per the frozen JSON,
      and the frozen discriminant string is ~204 decimal digits; disc(L),
      for the resolvent cubic's discriminant, is tied to Delta_E by
      repair_r3.resolvent_cubic_identity's corrected exact identity and is
      therefore comparably large, on the order of 10^200, i.e. roughly a
      664-bit quantity) -- NOT a claim that any computation was performed:
      the best presently known algorithms for computing class groups and
      unit groups of a number field (Buchmann-type index-calculus methods,
      Hafner-McCurley, and their GRH-conditional accelerations) run in
      SUBEXPONENTIAL time in the field's discriminant, L_disc[1/2, c]-type
      complexity (recalled, standard computational algebraic number theory;
      Cohen ACANT ch. 6, Buchmann 1990). At a ~664-bit discriminant, this
      subexponential cost is of the SAME ORDER OF DIFFICULTY as factoring an
      RSA modulus or solving a discrete log problem of comparable bit
      length -- i.e., precisely the class of problem this research program
      studies as currently intractable at cryptographic scale. Unconditional
      algorithms (avoiding GRH) are categorically worse, typically requiring
      an explicit Minkowski-bound ideal enumeration whose bound itself grows
      with sqrt(disc(L)), which at this scale is astronomically larger still.
      THIS FINDING IS A DESIGN-TIME ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASURED RESULT: no
      dry-run cost probe for the class-group computation has been run (that
      would be execution, forbidden in this task), and a future
      Coordinator-authorized bounded probe could in principle contradict
      this estimate (e.g. if L happens to have h(L) = 1, which is not
      determinable without running the probe). It is recorded here as the
      honest expectation, not as a proven impossibility.
    decidable_fallback_stage_a_prime_repaired: >-
      WHAT REMAINS DECIDABLE, restructuring Stage A into three gated
      sub-stages, replacing the predecessor's single-stage
      enumeration_order/halting_condition/decision_gate wholesale:
      Stage A'.0 (cheap, unconditional): compute the signature (r1,r2) of L
      via Sturm's-theorem sign-counting on the real roots of the resolvent
      cubic (an elementary, finite computation, no number-field algorithm
      needed), fixing rank(O_L^*) in closed form with no class-group work.
      Stage A'.1 (bounded-effort, may fail): attempt to compute h(L) and
      Cl(L)[2] (or at minimum, whether each prime of S_L is principal, and
      if not, a generator of the appropriate power) via a DECLARED,
      BUDGETED class-group/unit-group computation. If this bound is
      exhausted before completion -- EXPECTED at curve 302's scale per
      feasibility_finding_stated_plainly above, but never assumed without
      running the bounded attempt -- Stage A' reports "class group and
      S-unit generating set undetermined within declared budget" (an
      honest, scoped, non-mathematical-evidence outcome, AGENTS.md rule 3)
      and HALTS at this gate: Stage A'.2 does not run and READING (a)
      closure is UNREACHABLE via this route for curve 302.
      Stage A'.2 (only if A'.1 succeeds): full L(S,2) enumeration with
      explicit generators from generating_set_specification, local
      solubility testing exactly as the predecessor's enumeration_order
      described for the S_L-generated part, extended over the full
      generating set; produces an EXACT dim Sel_2(E), and READING (a) /
      READING (b) apply exactly as the predecessor's idea.claim states
      (decision_rule_integrity below).
      Stage A'.3 (always available, regardless of A'.1's outcome): the
      predecessor's ORIGINAL literal S_L-bitvector procedure is RETAINED but
      RELABELED HONESTLY as testing only the SUBGROUP W of L(S,2) generated
      by the S_L-prime classes that are individually principal (each
      non-principal prime's class is simply DROPPED from W, shrinking it
      further rather than corrupting it), producing an UNCONDITIONAL LOWER
      BOUND: dim(W) <= dim Sel_2(E) <= dim L(S,2). This lower bound CAN
      license Stage B (READING (b)'s search-licensing half only) if
      dim(W tested everywhere-locally-soluble) already reaches 32, but it
      CAN NEVER be used for READING (a) closure, since it may miss classes
      exactly as J1 found for the predecessor's original procedure.
    interaction_with_r2: >-
      Stage A'.1/A'.2's enumeration size and Stage A'.3's fallback size both
      depend on |S_L|, which repair_r2.corrected_prime_set_construction
      below fixes at <= 60 (not the predecessor's <= 63); this repair's cost
      model uses the corrected bound.
    added_interpretation_limit: >-
      ADDITIVE to protocol.interpretation_limits (inherited unchanged, not
      replaced): a negative or undetermined Stage A'.1 outcome is NEVER
      evidence for or against rank 32 (AGENTS.md rule 3), and specifically
      is NOT the same non-result as a Stage A'.2 budget-ceiling halt on the
      enumeration itself -- the two failure points (class-group computation
      vs. local-solubility enumeration) must be reported distinctly, since a
      reader conflating them could wrongly believe the enumeration itself
      was attempted and failed rather than never having reached the
      enumeration stage.
    what_remains_open: >-
      Whether Stage A'.1 is actually tractable for curve 302's real L is
      OPEN and cannot be resolved without running the bounded probe
      (explicitly out of scope for this zero-execution repair). If it is
      confirmed intractable, whether any alternative unconditional route to
      Cl(L)[2] exists at this scale (e.g. analytic bounds, partial descent-
      compatible workarounds, or accepting a GRH-conditional generating set
      with an explicit heuristic flag rather than an unconditional one) is
      an OPEN design question, deferred to a future proposal rather than
      resolved here.
